label: New York — departure

label: Seattle — rail/sea interchange

label: Dawson — three days
sources: [{"ref": "pub_bamnh26", "locator": "p.88 via PI timeline"}]
why: Arrival and duration stated (via PI). How LSQ travelled from Seattle to Dawson is not described in the provided material.

label: Fort Gibbon — parts from Grant
sources: [{"ref": "pub_bamnh26", "locator": "p.89 via PI: 'LSQ continues on to Fort Gibbon; Grant to Fairbanks'"}]
why: Stated via PI. The PI's phrasing ('continues on to') leaves the exact arrival day open; 25 July is the PI's entry date.

label: The Palisades — 'a high cut bank' examined
date_text: listed under 25 July 1907 by the PI; before 29 July
sources: [{"ref": "pub_bamnh26", "locator": "p.89 via PI: 'LSQ examines the Palisades (\"a high cut bank\" on the Yukon 35 miles below mouth of Tanana)'"}]
why: Place verified by GNIS and by LSQ's distance statement; the day of the examination is not separately stated.

label: St Michael
date_text: steams to St Michaels 29 July 1907; leaves for Nome 4 August
sources: [{"ref": "pub_bamnh26", "locator": "p.89 via PI"}]
why: Both dates stated (via PI).

label: Nome — five days; the claimants
date_text: tug from St Michael, 4 August (15 hours); 'in Nome for five days'; leaves 13 August 1907
sources: [{"ref": "pub_bamnh26", "locator": "p.89 via PI: tug 15 hours; five days; Startsman/Graham 'would make no reasonable agreement as to showing the body'"}, {"ref": "tale", "locator": "'arriving there a month later'"}]
why: 'Five days' and the 13 August departure do not quite fill 4–13 August; the Bulletin's own wording was not available to resolve this. Flagged in findings.

label: Solomon River — short trip, '30 mi to the east'
sources: [{"ref": "pub_bamnh26", "locator": "p.89 via PI: 'makes short trip up Solomon R., 30 mi to the east'"}]
why: Side trip from Nome; day unstated.

label: Keewalik ('the spit') — boat and helper found
date_text: leaves Nome on 'Corwin' 13 August; 'several unavoidable delays'; leaves Keewalik 24 August 1907
sources: [{"ref": "pub_bamnh26", "locator": "p.89 via PI: 'sailed to Keewalik at the eastern end of Kotzebue Sound'; canoe 'finally secured only by chance'; Jim Hoffman engaged 'for cook and helper'; 'Keewalik's three launches were under contract'"}]
why: Arrival day at Keewalik is not stated; the window runs from the Nome departure to the stated Keewalik departure.

label: Candle — visited, 'a few miles up Keewalik River'
sources: [{"ref": "pub_bamnh26", "locator": "p.89 via PI: 'visited Candle ... and then returned “to ‘the spit.’”'"}]
why: Side trip; day unstated.

label: Elephant Point — the find
date_text: leave Keewalik 24 August; at the bluff until the Bay began to freeze (19 September 1907)
sources: [{"ref": "pub_bamnh26", "locator": "p.89–90 via PI; Tale quoting p.90: 'portions of a mammoth skeleton together with some skin and hair...embedded...'"}, {"ref": "d_19080225_unsigned_osborn", "locator": "'Mr. Quackenbush found portions of a mammoth protruding from the frozen ground'"}]
why: Arrival date at the Point is not stated; the Buckland excursion (1 Sept) interrupts the stay. The excavation spot within the bluff is not located.

label: Buckland River — 15 miles, 'unusually early fall'
sources: [{"ref": "pub_bamnh26", "locator": "p.89 via PI: 'only go 15 mi due to unusually early fall'"}, {"ref": "d_19080327_quackenbush_bumpus_plan", "locator": "'I found bones of the mammoth, horse, bison, and caribou on the lower part of the Buckland River'"}]
why: Entry date stated; the 15-mile limit is LSQ's figure; the turning point is not plotted separately.

label: Keewalik — return; 'mining operations in interior ceased'
date_text: return to Keewalik 19 September 1907; takes 'Corwin' back to Nome (date not stated)
sources: [{"ref": "pub_bamnh26", "locator": "p.90 via PI"}]
why: Return date stated; departure on the Corwin undated.

label: Nome — 'first boat to Seattle'
sources: [{"ref": "pub_bamnh26", "locator": "p.90 via PI: 'Takes Corwin back to Nome, and first boat to Seattle'"}]
why: Only the sequence is attested.

label: Seattle — Ranier Grande Hotel
sources: [{"ref": "d_19071028_bumpus_quackenbush", "locator": "addressed to 'LSQ at the Ranier Grande Hotel, Seattle, Wash.': 'Have wired one hundred and fifty. Do you need more?'"}]
why: Presence in Seattle on this date attested by the addressed copy.

label: New York — return
date_text: 2 November 1907, 'owing to the inevitable delays in Alaskan travel'
sources: [{"ref": "pub_bamnh26", "locator": "p.90 via PI"}, {"ref": "tale", "locator": "'after he returned to New York in early November'"}]
why: Stated via PI.

label: New York — departure via Montreal
date_text: 19 May 1908 (letter); 'toward the end of May' (Bulletin via PI)

why: Three archival statements give 19 May; the Bulletin (as summarised by the PI) says 'toward the end of May'. Both are shown.

label: Montreal — Canadian Pacific routing
date_text: c. 20 May 1908 (inferred from the 19 May evening departure)
sources: [{"ref": "d_19080519_quackenbush_bumpus", "locator": "'via Montreal and the Canadian Pacific'"}]
why: Routing attested; no stop is described.

label: Seattle — Rainier Grand Hotel; sails on the 'Umatilla'
date_text: letter from Seattle 3 June; sails 4 June 1908
sources: [{"ref": "d_19080603_quackenbush_bumpus", "locator": "'Sails for Nome tomorrow afternoon on the Umatilla'; canoe arrived"}, {"ref": "d_19080519_quackenbush_bumpus", "locator": "'I sail from Seattle on the \"Umatilla\" on June 4th'"}, {"ref": "d_19081001_quackenbush_bumpus_report", "locator": "'I left Seattle by steamer on June 4th'"}]
why: Arrival day in Seattle not stated; departure stated three times.

label: Nome — 'ten days' delay in the ice'
date_text: arrives 21 June 1908; leaves 'in such a hurry' (day not stated)
sources: [{"ref": "pub_bamnh26", "locator": "p.90 via PI: 'LSQ arrives Nome \"after ten days' delay in the ice\"'"}, {"ref": "d_19081001_quackenbush_bumpus_report", "locator": "'did not reach Nome until June 21st'"}, {"ref": "d_19080624_quackenbush_bumpus", "locator": "'the trip from Seattle to Nome occupied seventeen days'"}]
why: Arrival stated; departure inferred as immediate ('I left Nome in such a hurry').

label: Lane's Landing / Shelton — head of the railroad
sources: [{"ref": "d_19080624_quackenbush_bumpus", "locator": "'I am now at the head of the railroad and on my way across the Seward Peninsula to Candle'"}, {"ref": "pub_bamnh26", "locator": "p.90 via PI: 'Crosses Seward Pen by train to Shelton, wagon to Candle'"}, {"ref": "d_19081001_quackenbush_bumpus_report", "locator": "'the head of the Seward Peninsula R.R. at Lane's Landing'"}]
why: The place carries two attested names for one gazetteer point (see place record); the flag records naming variance, not a dispute about position.

label: Candle — Hoffman and his dory engaged
date_text: c. 25/26–29 June 1908 (crossing 'four and one half days' from Nome; rowed to Keewalik 29 June)
sources: [{"ref": "d_19081001_quackenbush_bumpus_report", "locator": "'The crossing from Nome to Candle occupied four and one half days'; 'At Candle I engaged a man to act as cook and assistant and also hired his fishing dory'; 'On June 29th we rowed down the Keewalik River to Keewalik'"}, {"ref": "d_19080624_quackenbush_bumpus", "locator": "'Candle where I hope to be in four or five days'"}]
why: Arrival at Candle computed from the report's 4.5-day crossing; LSQ's letter of 24 June expected 4–5 more days from Lane's Landing, which does not agree (see findings).

label: Keewalik — ice 'blown in again from the Arctic ocean'
sources: [{"ref": "d_19081001_quackenbush_bumpus_report", "locator": "'On June 29th we rowed down the Keewalik River to Keewalik'; 'On July 1st I started for Elephant Point in the dory'"}, {"ref": "d_19080701_quackenbush_bumpus", "locator": "letter from Keewalik, 1 July 1908"}, {"ref": "pub_bamnh26", "locator": "p.90 via PI: '1 July 1908: LSQ & Hoffman leave Keewalik'"}]
why: Both dates stated.

label: Elephant Point — excavation by hand
date_text: reached 3 July; excavation from 4 July; ice out 10 July; finished before 20 July 1908 (end date not stated)
sources: [{"ref": "d_19081001_quackenbush_bumpus_report", "locator": "'reached Elephant Point on July 3rd; the mammoth remains had not been disturbed. Excavation was commenced on the 4th'"}, {"ref": "pub_bamnh26", "locator": "p.90 via PI: ice 'finally' breaks up 10 July; 'Excavate mammoth by hand'"}, {"ref": "tale", "locator": "'commenced excavation \"with picks,\" and within a few days could tell that the skeleton was, \"unfortunately,\" incomplete'"}]
why: Start stated; the end of the excavation is bounded only by the 20 July departure from Keewalik.

label: Cut bluff near Choris Peninsula — fossils gathered
date_text: after the excavation and before 20 July 1908 (day not stated)
sources: [{"ref": "d_19081001_quackenbush_bumpus_report", "locator": "'I crossed Eschscholtz Bay to a cut bluff on the north side near Choris Peninsula. After gathering some fossils here I returned to Keewalik'"}]
why: Position approximate (see place); day unstated.

label: Keewalik — boxes built, collection packed
date_text: before 20 July 1908 (arrival day not stated); the first boat of the season arrived 'two weeks' after 29 June with the canoe
sources: [{"ref": "d_19081001_quackenbush_bumpus_report", "locator": "'returned to Keewalik, built boxes, packed the collection, and prepared for an expedition up the Buckland River'; 'The first boat of the season did not reach Keewalik until two weeks later; she brought a canoe'"}, {"ref": "pub_bamnh26", "locator": "p.91 via PI: '20 July 1908: LSQ & Hoffman leave Keewalik for Buckland R.'"}]
why: Departure stated; arrival inferred.

label: Buckland River mouth — dory with canoe in tow
date_text: left Keewalik 20 July; dory anchored 8 miles up on the morning of 22 July 1908
sources: [{"ref": "d_19081001_quackenbush_bumpus_report", "locator": "'left Keewalik in the day, with the canoe in tow, on July 20th. In the morning of the 22nd the dory was anchored 8 miles up the river'"}]
why: Stated.

sources: [{"ref": "d_19081001_quackenbush_bumpus_report", "locator": "as above"}, {"ref": "pi_timeline", "locator": "'22 July 1908: LSQ & Hoffman anchor the dory 8 miles up the Buckland, \"take to the canoe.\"'"}]
why: Date stated; position approximate (river miles).

sources: [{"ref": "d_19081001_quackenbush_bumpus_report", "locator": "'one such deposit at the lower end of a broad basin — 62 miles up the river — is fully one hundred feet thick'"}]
why: Position approximate; day unstated.

sources: [{"ref": "d_19081001_quackenbush_bumpus_report", "locator": "'On July 28th I reached a point estimated at 86 miles above the mouth of the river and could go no further with the canoe. I walked a few miles higher'"}, {"ref": "tale", "locator": "'Quackenbush and Hoffman turned back about 80 miles inland'"}]
why: Date stated; distance disputed between the two provided sources (86 vs 'about 80').

label: West Fork — ascended 'a few miles'
sources: [{"ref": "d_19081001_quackenbush_bumpus_report", "locator": "'On the return trip I ascended the West Fork a few miles'"}]
why: Day unstated.

label: Buckland River mouth — back to the dory
sources: [{"ref": "d_19081001_quackenbush_bumpus_report", "locator": "'on August 5th reached the mouth of the river'; 'Here I transferred the outfit to the dory'"}]
why: Stated.

sources: [{"ref": "d_19081001_quackenbush_bumpus_report", "locator": "'crossed the Buckland estuary to the extreme eastern end of Eschscholtz Bay to examine a small stream where \"mud\" banks were reported by Beechey in 1826, but found sand bluffs and no fossils'"}]
why: Stream unnamed; placed approximately.

sources: [{"ref": "d_19081001_quackenbush_bumpus_report", "locator": "'I next cruised along the south shore of Eschscholtz Bay from the mouth of the Buckland westward past Elephant Point to the end of the silt deposit and collected a few more fossils'"}]

sources: [{"ref": "d_19081001_quackenbush_bumpus_report", "locator": "'On August 11th I crossed to the north shore of Eschscholtz Bay, and on the following morning, leaving the boats, we set out on foot with likght [sic] packs and crossed Hotham Peninsula to Hotham Inlet'"}]

sources: [{"ref": "d_19081001_quackenbush_bumpus_report", "locator": "'Four days were spent in examining parts of the south shore of Selawik Lake and the southern and western shores of Hotham Inlet ... almost barren of fossils'"}]
why: Duration stated; exact shores examined not located.

sources: [{"ref": "d_19081001_quackenbush_bumpus_report", "locator": "'On August 17th we recrossed Hotham Peninsula to Eschscholtz Bay where we were delayed by a storm'"}]

sources: [{"ref": "d_19081001_quackenbush_bumpus_report", "locator": "'On August 20th I returned to Keewalik'; 'took the first boat for Nome (on August 29th)'; canoe 'stored in the warehouse of the Keewalik Hotel ... left in charge of Mr. Ferdinand Quinn'"}, {"ref": "pub_bamnh26", "locator": "p.91 via PI: '20 August 1908: LSQ & Hoffman sail back to Keewalik'"}]
